pairs: so that you may not be judged.
For with whatever judgment you judge,
et in qua mensura mensi fueritis,
and with whatever measure you measure out,
so shall it be measured back to you.
Quid autem vides festucam in oculo fratris tui,
And how can you see the splinter in your brother’s eye,
et trabem in oculo tuo non vides?
and not see the board in your own eye?
Or how can you say to your brother,
Sine ejiciam festucam de oculo tuo,
‘Let me take the splinter from your eye,’
et ecce trabs est in oculo tuo?
while, behold, a board is in your own eye?
ejice primum trabem de oculo tuo,
first remove the board from your own eye,
et tunc videbis ejicere festucam de oculo fratris tui.
and then you will see clearly enough to remove the splinter from your brother’s eye.
Do not give what is holy to dogs,
neque mittatis margaritas vestras ante porcos,
and do not cast your pearls before swine,
ne forte conculcent eas pedibus suis,
lest perhaps they may trample them under their feet, and then,
turning, they may tear you apart.
and it shall be given to you.
and it shall be opened to you.
and to anyone who knocks, it will be opened.
Aut quis est ex vobis homo,
Or what man is there among you,
quem si petierit filius suus panem,
who, if his son were to ask him for bread,
or if he were to ask him for a fish,
nostis bona data dare filiis vestris:
know how to give good gifts to your sons,
how much more will your Father,
qui in cælis est, dabit bona petentibus se?
who is in heaven, give good things to those who ask him?
Omnia ergo quæcumque vultis ut faciant vobis homines,
all things whatsoever that you wish that men would do to you,
For this is the law and the prophets.
et multi sunt qui intrant per eam.
and many there are who enter through it.
and how straight is the way,
et pauci sunt qui inveniunt eam!
and few there are who find it!
qui veniunt ad vos in vestimentis ovium,
who come to you in sheep’s clothing,
You shall know them by their fruits.
Can grapes be gathered from thorns,
Sic omnis arbor bona fructus bonos facit:
So then, every good tree produces good fruit,
mala autem arbor malos fructus facit.
and the evil tree produces evil fruit.
Non potest arbor bona malos fructus facere:
A good tree is not able to produce evil fruit,
neque arbor mala bonos fructus facere.
and an evil tree is not able to produce good fruit.
Omnis arbor, quæ non facit fructum bonum, excidetur, et in ignem mittetur.
Every tree which does not produce good fruit shall be cut down and cast into the fire.
Igitur ex fructibus eorum cognoscetis eos.
Therefore, by their fruits you will know them.
Not all who say to me,
will enter into the kingdom of heaven.
sed qui facit voluntatem Patris mei,
But whoever does the will of my Father,
the same shall enter into the kingdom of heaven.
Multi dicent mihi in illa die:
Many will say to me in that day,
did we not prophesy in your name,
et in nomine tuo dæmonia ejecimus,
and cast out demons in your name,
et in nomine tuo virtutes multas fecimus?
and perform many powerful deeds in your name?’
And then will I disclose to them:
Omnis ergo qui audit verba mea hæc,
everyone who hears these words of mine
and does them shall be compared to a wise man,
qui ædificavit domum suam supra petram,
who built his house upon the rock.
for it was founded on the rock.
Et omnis qui audit verba mea hæc, et non facit ea, similis erit viro stulto,
And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them shall be like a foolish man,
qui ædificavit domum suam super arenam:
who built his house upon the sand.
when Jesus had completed these words,
that the crowds were astonished at his doctrine.
Erat enim docens eos sicut potestatem habens,
For he was teaching them as one who has authority,
